findings.text: the done-when requires "the new command and the transition alias report the same revision" on the renamed scratch tree, but §10 is the only section that delivers the alias ("the old command kept only as a transition alias") and §10 declares its own wait on `s21`, while `s21`'s Delivers names a rename of "the distribution and commands" and no alias at all, so the tree the section describes yields `iter-codex` alone and the clause can only pass by building a surface the plan assigns to a deferred section, whose own removal-by-zero-consumer rule then conflicts with the closing search for old-name references

findings.reason: without a durable home the deferred package rename has to re-derive the rename (and the kept-name reasons) from nothing, which is the work this section exists to do once and prove.
findings.text: the done-when ends by removing "the scratch copies and the scratch environment", while the section's deliverable is one repeatable rename plus a kept-name list that `s10` and `s11` declare themselves dependent on, and no tracked or durable path is named for either artifact, so the thing two later sections consume has no stated existence after the rehearsal ends and cannot be re-run by a later reader
